frontMatter.title: Culturally Inspired Contemplative Tarot
frontMatter.subtitle: A 78-card guide for reflection, journaling, and careful conversation

sections.title: About this deck
sections.body: This deck uses the familiar 78-card tarot framework: twenty-two Core Arcana cards explore broad human thresholds, while four fourteen-card suits consider thought and language, emotion and relationship, discernment and boundaries, and material life and stewardship. Its visual vocabulary is culturally inspired by varied West, Central, and South Asian arts of geometry, gardens, manuscripts, courtyards, textiles, metalwork, and attentive craft. These references are creative influences, not a claim to represent a single culture, community, period, or religious tradition.

sections.title: How to use the cards
sections.body: Choose a card deliberately or at random as a prompt, not an answer. First describe what you notice without interpreting it. Read the card theme and invitation; then test the out-of-balance passage against your actual circumstances. Journal with the question, try the small practice, and revise the intention into language you can genuinely act on. In groups, let each person interpret their own experience and decline any question. Decisions should still rely on evidence, consent, professional advice where needed, and direct conversation with affected people.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The cards do not predict events, reveal hidden facts, access the unseen, confer religious authority, prescribe ritual, diagnose health, replace professional care, or guarantee outcomes. They do not make desired outcomes happen by symbolic force. No image, title, subtitle, or interpretation should be treated as scripture, doctrine, omen, command, or proof. If a prompt increases fear, compulsion, or certainty about another person's private motives, set it aside and return to verifiable information and appropriate support.

sections.title: Language and titles
sections.body: Non-English subtitles are retained as poetic companions to the English titles. They require review by fluent speakers and culturally informed editors before publication. They carry no doctrinal status and should not be used to teach language, theology, or religious practice. Several choices are explicitly flagged in the accompanying QA report rather than presented as settled or authoritative.

sections.title: A note on care
sections.body: Cultural inspiration asks for specificity, credit, and revision—not a generalized atmosphere of an imagined ‘East.’ Future art and language review should identify the actual region, period, object, and community behind a reference; avoid sacred figures and events, decorative scripture, and ritual prescriptions; and invite readers from relevant cultures to challenge conflations or inaccuracies.

frontMatter.closingNote: Use as a reflective prompt; keep decisions grounded in evidence, consent, and appropriate support.
frontMatter.footer: For contemplation, not prediction, religious guidance, or claims about the unseen.

guide.theme: beginning, trust, willingness to enter the path
guide.descriptionOfImage: The image shows an anonymous seeker in a flowing ivory cloak standing on a high desert ridge before dawn, one hand raised toward a narrow horizon of gold, fabric moving gently in the night wind, a small path beginning behind the figure, faint geometric constellations across the sky. The artwork uses a vertical composition, decorative border, and open lower cartouche. No readable text appears in the scene.
guide.invitation: A beginning does not need to prove where it will end. This card invites a modest experiment: enough courage to move, enough humility to revise, and enough care to notice who may be affected by the step.
guide.outOfBalance: Curiosity can become avoidant novelty: many starts, no accountability, and risk mistaken for freedom.
guide.contemplate: What would it mean to enter the path without needing the path to promise a destination?
guide.practice: Write the smallest reversible next step and the boundary that would keep it responsible. For The Seeker, apply the exercise specifically to beginning, trust, willingness to enter the path. Return after a short pause and revise anything that sounds absolute.
guide.intention: I will meet beginning, trust, willingness to enter the path with honesty, proportion, and one concrete act that respects both my limits and other people's dignity.
guide.visualMeditation: Move your attention between the path and the cloak. Notice distance, tension, or exchange between them. What relationship within you does that movement bring into focus?

guide.outOfBalance: Skill can become performance, manipulation, or the belief that having words means having wisdom.
guide.contemplate: Where can the tools around the pen increase agency, and where might they be used to control?

guide.theme: cycles, changing conditions, ease and hardship, changing conditions
guide.descriptionOfImage: The image shows a monumental brass astrolabe with concentric rings turning above a desert observatory floor, four seasonal winds suggested by sand, rain, petals, and dry leaves circling the mechanism, cosmic indigo sky. The artwork uses a vertical composition, decorative border, and open lower cartouche. No readable text appears in the scene.
guide.invitation: Conditions turn, sometimes through choice and sometimes beyond it. The invitation is to release the fantasy of total control while identifying the small, consequential part that still belongs to you.
guide.outOfBalance: Acceptance can become passivity, while agency can become self-blame for conditions no person could control.

guide.outOfBalance: Fair measure can become punitive exactness, abstraction, or confidence that ignores unequal starting points.
